title: the measurement behind the discovery pivot is stale or no longer adds up
evidence: newest account-level reach attribution 11.3h ago: non-follower=0 follower=4 total=4 -- the newest account-level reach attribution is 11.3h old (bound 6h). Producer: Growth::MetricsCollector#fetch_reach_attribution, hourly via growth:snapshot_followers, BEST-EFFORT by design (a failed insights call is logged once and stored as NULL). The pivot's justification -- that non-follower reach is a measured zero, so no content lever can move followers -- is only as good as this row: stale, it is a claim about the past; a missing or non-reconciling breakdown makes it a MISSING DIMENSION rather than a measured zero.

notes.note: FIXED root cause: producer cadence mismatch. The growth-brain snapshots every 12h, so reach attribution went stale up to 12h and tripped the 6h bound. Added growth:snapshot_followers to bin/scheduled_posting.sh (hourly posting driver, user crontab) as a NON-FATAL step following the existing PIPESTATUS-WARN pattern, matching the check's documented hourly cadence. VERIFIED: ran growth:snapshot_followers live -> 'Snapshot recorded: 159 followers'; newest growth_snapshots row id 1181 taken_at 2026-10-10 06:02:48 with reach attribution populated non_follower=0 follower=5 total=5 (fresh, reconciles). Check now sees <1h-old attribution and stops firing; measurement stays fresh hourly.
